input.quote: 14.1 Indemnification by RevMed. RevMed shall indemnify, defend and hold harmless Sanofi, its Affiliates and their respective officers, directors, agents and employees (\"Sanofi Indemnitees\") from and against any Third Party Claims and Losses arising therefrom under or related to this Agreement against any of them to the extent arising or resulting from:
input.rationale: Section 14.1 gives us a RevMed indemnity for (a) RevMed's negligence/recklessness/willful misconduct, (b) breach of its representations and warranties, and (c) breach of its obligations, with standard procedure, notice, control and cooperation in Section 14.3, and Section 14.5 confirms the liability cap/consequential waiver does not cut back indemnities. However, it contains no head of indemnity for third-party claims that the licensed technology or the Products infringe or misappropriate third-party IP. IP infringement risk is only picked up indirectly via breach of the Article XIII IP warranties, most of which are knowledge-qualified and given only as of the Execution Date (e.g. p0549 "To RevMed's Knowledge... does not infringe"), while Section 14.2(a) affirmatively puts third-party claims arising from our Research, Development, Manufacture and Commercialization of Products on us. Section 10.7 only gives us a first right to negotiate a third-party licence at our own cost. Under the detection guidance this fails the fallback (Vendor indemnity excluding IP infringement), so we propose the minimal addition of an express IP infringement head as new Section 14.1(d), leaving RevMed's existing carve-outs for our own negligence and breaches intact.

proposal.summary: Add a RevMed third-party IP infringement indemnity to Section 14.1
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 14.1 covers only RevMed's misconduct and its breaches, so a third-party claim that the licensed technology or the Products infringe IP falls on us (and is even swept into our indemnity in Section 14.2(a)). We have added an express RevMed IP infringement indemnity, consistent with our playbook requirement that the licensor stand behind third-party IP claims relating to the technology it licenses; RevMed remains protected by the existing carve-outs for our own negligence and breaches.
